records.title: Fra Mauro world map: supplied reproduction
records.note: South-up Fra Mauro cartography. The exact supplied reproduction edition is not established. Alternative image of an existing Atlas map, not a newly identified historical object.
records.rights: Public-domain underlying historical artwork; exact supplied reproduction provenance unverified
records.credit: Fra Mauro; underlying work held by Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana. User-supplied reproduction.

records.title: Kangnido world map: supplied reproduction
records.depicted: Korean court geographical synthesis, not universal knowledge
records.note: The image represents the Kangnido tradition. The app already contains this map identity. It is not asserted to be the lost 1402 original.
records.rights: Public-domain historical work and comparable PD-Art reproduction; exact supplied copy unverified
records.credit: Kangnido tradition; Kim Sa-hyeong, Yi Mu and Yi Hoe. User-supplied reproduction.

records.title: Orbis terrarum antiquis notus
records.note: The title, imprint and insets match Kiepert's 1892 Atlas antiquus plate I, catalogue 11690.003. The Eratosthenes and Ptolemy insets are later historical reconstructions, not ancient original maps.
records.rights: David Rumsey Map Collection permits credited non-commercial digital reproduction; reassess before commercial use
records.credit: David Rumsey Map Collection, David Rumsey Map Center, Stanford Libraries. Heinrich Kiepert, 1892.

records.title: Imperiorum Antiquorum
records.note: Robert Wilkinson's historical atlas combines geography and a synchronistic table. Its publication date is 1800, not the ancient periods described.
records.rights: Public-domain historical plate; catalogue comparison permits free reuse of scans
records.credit: Robert Wilkinson, 1800. Catalogue comparison: Geographicus Rare Antique Maps. User-supplied scan.

records.title: How Japan Could Attack U.S.
records.depicted: Hypothetical scenario, not an attack that occurred
records.note: Visible masthead and title match Howard Burke catalogue material. Target insets and arrows are journalistic speculation, not verified Japanese operational plans.
records.rights: Commons records US public domain by non-renewal; permission outside the US unestablished. Link only.
records.credit: Howard Burke; Los Angeles Examiner; Cornell Persuasive Cartography.
records.warning: Hypothetical newspaper map. Not an actual invasion or territorial control record.

records.title: If We Enter a World War - and LOSE!
records.depicted: Imagined partition of the United States
records.note: This is a hypothetical newspaper illustration. The supplied masthead identifies the Chicago edition; it is not evidence of an actual partition.
records.credit: Howard Austin Burke attribution in catalogue; Chicago Herald and Examiner.
records.warning: Imagined scenario, not an historical invasion.

records.title: Alexander campaigns: French reconstruction
records.publication: Modern; visible Brill historical atlas credit, 2009
records.note: The legend separates campaigns, conquered cities, claimed territories and other categories. Do not flatten these into one verified boundary. Visible modern publisher credit requires a reuse check.

records.title: Assyrian expansion and campaigns: German reconstruction
records.note: The legend depicts multiple reigns and campaigns. It supplies no single independently verified geographical boundary or date.
records.warning: Multiple time layers, not a single-year map.

records.title: Decorative classical-world map: unidentified edition
records.note: An aged parchment aesthetic and Latin labels do not establish ancient provenance. Similar subject to another supplied decorative map but not a proven duplicate.

records.title: Sasanian / Gupta region map with inconsistent labels
records.depicted: Mixed periods; unsuitable as single-year reconstruction
records.note: The legend gives Gupta dates about 320-550 CE while the same Indian region is labelled Shunga 185-72 BCE. This internal chronology conflict prevents use as a contemporary political map.
records.warning: Chronology conflict: Gupta and Shunga belong to different periods. No time-specific territory layer.

records.title: Achaemenid Empire: French reconstruction
records.depicted: Imperial maximum extent, satrapies, royal road and battles
records.note: This is a modern reconstruction, not an Achaemenid-produced artefact. Maximum extent is not automatically applicable at every year.
records.warning: No historical boundary geometry inferred from raster.

records.title: The Empire of Alexander: relief reconstruction
records.note: Terrain-and-campaign reconstruction including different land and fleet routes. Same subject as the French Alexander map, not a duplicate image. Route validity and licence unverified.

records.depicted: Old place-names, not verified cartographic object
